q: How many edge locations does Amazon CloudFront have globally (approximate as of 2024)?

exp.a: CloudFront has far more than 50 edge locations.
exp.b: CloudFront has far more than 100 edge locations.
exp.c: Correct. Amazon CloudFront has 450+ Points of Presence (PoPs) including edge locations and Regional Edge Caches across the globe.
exp.d: CloudFront does not have 1000+ edge locations currently.

q: What is the default TTL (Time to Live) for CloudFront cached objects if no Cache-Control header is specified?

exp.a: The default TTL is not 1 hour.
exp.b: Correct. The default TTL for CloudFront is 24 hours (86,400 seconds) if no Cache-Control or Expires header is specified by the origin.
exp.c: 48 hours is not the default TTL.
exp.d: 7 days is not the default TTL.

q: What is the maximum file size that can be delivered through CloudFront using a single GET request?

exp.a: 5 GB is the limit for S3 single PUT, not CloudFront delivery.
exp.b: 10 GB is not the correct maximum file size for CloudFront.
exp.c: Correct. CloudFront can deliver files up to 20 GB in size using a single GET request.
exp.d: 30 GB exceeds CloudFront's maximum file size for a single GET request.

q: What is the maximum number of alternate domain names (CNAMEs) you can associate with a single CloudFront distribution?

exp.a: 10 is not the correct limit.
exp.b: 25 is not the correct limit.
exp.c: Correct. You can associate up to 100 alternate domain names (CNAMEs) with a single CloudFront distribution.
exp.d: 200 exceeds the default limit.

q: How many Regional Edge Cache locations does CloudFront have (approximate)?

exp.a: 5 is too few for CloudFront's Regional Edge Caches.
exp.b: Correct. CloudFront has approximately 13 Regional Edge Cache locations globally that sit between the origin and the edge locations.
exp.c: 50 is too many for Regional Edge Caches.
exp.d: 100 is the number closer to edge locations, not Regional Edge Caches.

q: How many invalidation paths can you submit per month at no additional charge?

exp.a: 100 is not the correct free tier for invalidation paths.
exp.b: 500 is not the correct free tier for invalidation paths.
exp.c: Correct. CloudFront provides 1,000 invalidation paths per month at no additional charge. After that, each path costs $0.005.
exp.d: 10,000 exceeds the free tier for invalidation paths.

q: What is the maximum execution time for CloudFront Functions?

exp.a: Correct. CloudFront Functions are designed to execute in sub-millisecond time (less than 1ms) and handle millions of requests per second for lightweight operations.
exp.b: 5 milliseconds is longer than the CloudFront Functions execution limit.
exp.c: 5 seconds is the limit for Lambda@Edge on viewer events.
exp.d: 30 seconds is the limit for Lambda@Edge on origin events.

q: What is the maximum execution time for Lambda@Edge on origin-facing events (origin request/response)?

exp.a: 5 seconds is the limit for viewer-facing events, not origin events.
exp.b: 15 seconds is not the correct limit.
exp.c: Correct. Lambda@Edge functions triggered by origin request or origin response events can run for up to 30 seconds.
exp.d: 60 seconds exceeds the Lambda@Edge timeout for origin events.

q: What is the maximum execution time for Lambda@Edge on viewer-facing events (viewer request/response)?

exp.a: 1 second is not the correct limit for viewer events.
exp.b: Correct. Lambda@Edge functions triggered by viewer request or viewer response events can run for up to 5 seconds.
exp.c: 15 seconds is not the correct limit.
exp.d: 30 seconds is the limit for origin events, not viewer events.

q: What is the maximum memory for Lambda@Edge functions?

exp.a: 128 MB is the minimum memory, not maximum.
exp.b: 256 MB is not the maximum.
exp.c: 512 MB is not the maximum.
exp.d: Correct. Lambda@Edge functions can use up to 10,240 MB (10 GB) of memory for origin-facing events.

q: What is the maximum package size for CloudFront Functions?

exp.a: 2 KB is too small for CloudFront Functions.
exp.b: Correct. CloudFront Functions have a maximum package size of 10 KB.
exp.c: 1 MB is the limit for Lambda@Edge viewer events.
exp.d: 50 MB is the limit for Lambda@Edge origin events.

q: What is the CloudFront free tier for data transfer out per month?

exp.a: Correct. CloudFront offers 1 TB of data transfer out to the internet per month as part of the always-free tier (not limited to 12 months).
exp.b: 50 GB is not the correct free tier amount.
exp.c: 10 GB is not the correct free tier amount.
exp.d: 100 GB is not the correct free tier amount.

q: How many HTTP/HTTPS requests are included in the CloudFront free tier per month?

exp.a: 1 million is not the correct free tier amount.
exp.b: 2 million is not the correct free tier amount.
exp.c: Correct. CloudFront free tier includes 10,000,000 HTTP/HTTPS requests per month.
exp.d: 100 million exceeds the free tier allowance.

q: What is the maximum number of origins you can configure per CloudFront distribution?

exp.a: 10 is not the default limit for origins.
exp.b: Correct. By default, you can have up to 25 origins per CloudFront distribution (can be increased via service quota request).
exp.c: 50 is not the default limit.
exp.d: 100 is not the default limit.

q: What is the maximum number of cache behaviors per CloudFront distribution?

exp.a: 10 is not the default limit.
exp.b: Correct. By default, you can have up to 25 cache behaviors per CloudFront distribution (can be increased).
exp.c: 50 is not the default limit.
exp.d: 100 is not the default limit.

q: What is the maximum number of CloudFront distributions per AWS account (default limit)?

exp.a: 25 is not the default limit for distributions.
exp.b: 100 is not the default limit for distributions.
exp.c: Correct. The default limit is 200 CloudFront distributions per AWS account, which can be increased by requesting a service quota increase.
exp.d: 500 exceeds the default limit.

q: What is the maximum TTL that can be set for a CloudFront cache behavior?

exp.a: 24 hours is the default TTL, not the maximum.
exp.b: 7 days is not the maximum TTL.
exp.c: 30 days is not the maximum TTL.
exp.d: Correct. The maximum TTL for CloudFront can be set up to 365 days (31,536,000 seconds).

q: What is the default minimum TTL that can be set for a CloudFront distribution?

exp.a: Correct. The minimum TTL can be set to 0 seconds, which means CloudFront will always check with the origin if the content is up to date (using conditional requests like If-Modified-Since).
exp.b: 60 seconds is not the minimum configurable TTL.
exp.c: 300 seconds is not the minimum configurable TTL.
exp.d: 3600 seconds is not the minimum configurable TTL.

q: What is CloudFront Functions' maximum memory allocation?

exp.a: Correct. CloudFront Functions are allocated a maximum of 2 MB of memory, keeping them lightweight for high-scale operations.
exp.b: 10 MB exceeds the CloudFront Functions memory limit.
exp.c: 128 MB is the minimum for Lambda@Edge.
exp.d: 256 MB exceeds CloudFront Functions limits.

q: What is the cost per invalidation path after exceeding the 1,000 free paths per month?

exp.a: $0.001 is too low.
exp.b: Correct. After the first 1,000 free invalidation paths per month, each additional path costs $0.005.
exp.c: $0.01 is not the correct price.
exp.d: $0.05 is too high.

q: How many concurrent invalidation requests can be in progress at the same time per distribution?

exp.a: You can have more than 1 concurrent invalidation.
exp.b: Correct. You can have up to 3 wildcard invalidation requests in progress at the same time per CloudFront distribution, or up to 3,000 individual file invalidation paths.
exp.c: 10 exceeds the concurrent limit.
exp.d: There is a defined limit.

q: What is the maximum body size for a request that Lambda@Edge can generate when intercepting viewer requests?

exp.a: 10 KB is too small.
exp.b: Correct. When Lambda@Edge generates a response directly (without forwarding to the origin) on viewer request/response events, the body is limited to 40 KB.
exp.c: 1 MB is the function package size limit for viewer events, not the body size.
exp.d: 5 MB exceeds the limit.

q: What is the connection timeout for CloudFront to origin (how long CloudFront waits to establish a connection)?

exp.a: 5 seconds is not the default.
exp.b: Correct. The default origin connection timeout is 10 seconds, and it can be configured between 1 and 10 seconds.
exp.c: 30 seconds is the origin response timeout, not connection timeout.
exp.d: 60 seconds exceeds the maximum connection timeout.

q: What is the default origin response timeout (how long CloudFront waits for a response from the origin)?

exp.a: 10 seconds is the connection timeout, not response timeout.
exp.b: Correct. The default origin response timeout is 30 seconds, configurable between 1 and 60 seconds (or up to 180 seconds with a quota increase).
exp.c: 60 seconds is the maximum without a quota increase, not the default.
exp.d: 120 seconds exceeds the default and requires special configuration.

q: What is CloudFront's origin connection attempts default value?

exp.a: 1 attempt is the minimum, not the default.
exp.b: 2 is not the default.
exp.c: Correct. CloudFront attempts to connect to the origin 3 times by default (configurable between 1 and 3) before either failing over to a secondary origin or returning an error.
exp.d: 5 exceeds the maximum connection attempts.

q: What is the maximum size of a Lambda@Edge function deployment package for origin-facing events?

exp.a: 1 MB is the limit for viewer-facing events.
exp.b: 5 MB is not the correct limit.
exp.c: Correct. Lambda@Edge functions for origin request/response events can have a deployment package up to 50 MB.
exp.d: 250 MB is the limit for regular Lambda with layers, not Lambda@Edge.

q: What is the maximum number of headers you can forward to the origin (whitelist) in a CloudFront cache behavior?

exp.a: 5 is too few.
exp.b: Correct. You can whitelist up to 10 headers to forward to the origin in a cache behavior (this can be increased via quota request).
exp.c: 30 exceeds the default limit.
exp.d: There is a defined limit on whitelisted headers.

q: What is the maximum number of SSL/TLS certificates you can associate with a CloudFront distribution?

exp.a: Correct. Each CloudFront distribution can have only 1 custom SSL/TLS certificate (from ACM or IAM) associated with it. However, that certificate can cover multiple domain names (SAN/wildcard).
exp.b: You cannot associate 2 certificates.
exp.c: 5 is not correct.
exp.d: 10 is not correct.

q: What is the monthly cost of using Dedicated IP Custom SSL with CloudFront?

exp.a: SNI Custom SSL is free, not Dedicated IP.
exp.b: $100/month is not the correct price.
exp.c: Correct. Dedicated IP Custom SSL costs $600/month per distribution. It's needed for legacy clients that don't support SNI.
exp.d: $1,000/month is not the correct price.

q: What is the maximum number of CloudFront Functions that can be created per AWS account?

exp.a: 10 is too low.
exp.b: 25 is too low.
exp.c: 50 is not the default limit.
exp.d: Correct. The default limit is 100 CloudFront Functions per AWS account (this can be increased via service quota request).

q: What is the maximum number of CloudFront distributions that can be associated with a single AWS WAF web ACL?

exp.a: Multiple distributions can share a web ACL.
exp.b: 10 is not the correct limit.
exp.c: Correct. A single AWS WAF web ACL can be associated with up to 100 CloudFront distributions.
exp.d: There is a limit of 100 distributions per web ACL.

q: What is the minimum rate limit threshold for a WAF rate-based rule?

exp.a: 10 is below the minimum threshold.
exp.b: Correct. The minimum rate limit for AWS WAF rate-based rules is 100 requests per 5-minute period.
exp.c: 500 is above the minimum.
exp.d: 2,000 is the default example but not the minimum.

q: What is the maximum number of IP addresses (or IP ranges) that can be included in a single AWS WAF IP set used with CloudFront?

exp.a: 100 is too low.
exp.b: 1,000 is not the correct limit.
exp.c: Correct. A single WAF IP set can contain up to 10,000 IP addresses or IP address ranges (CIDR blocks).
exp.d: 100,000 exceeds the limit.

q: What is the monthly cost of AWS Shield Advanced?

exp.a: $100/month is too low.
exp.b: $500/month is not correct.
exp.c: Correct. AWS Shield Advanced costs $3,000 per month per organization (with a 1-year commitment), plus data transfer fees.
exp.d: $10,000/month is too high.

q: What is the typical propagation time for a new CloudFront distribution to be deployed globally?

exp.a: Under 1 minute is too fast for global propagation.
exp.b: Correct. New CloudFront distributions or configuration changes typically propagate globally within 5-10 minutes.
exp.c: 1-2 hours is longer than typical propagation time.
exp.d: 24 hours is much longer than needed.

q: What is the maximum number of custom headers you can configure CloudFront to add to origin requests?

exp.a: 5 is not the limit.
exp.b: Correct. You can add up to 10 custom headers per origin in CloudFront that are sent with every request to that origin.
exp.c: 25 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: 50 exceeds the limit.

q: What is the minimum file size for CloudFront to apply compression?

exp.a: 100 bytes is too small; compression overhead would make it inefficient.
exp.b: Correct. CloudFront compresses files between 1,000 bytes and 10,000,000 bytes (10 MB) when compression is enabled and the viewer supports it.
exp.c: 10,000 bytes is not the minimum.
exp.d: 1 MB is far above the minimum.

q: What is the maximum file size that CloudFront will compress?

exp.a: 1 MB is below the maximum.
exp.b: 5 MB is below the maximum.
exp.c: Correct. CloudFront will compress files up to 10,000,000 bytes (10 MB). Files larger than 10 MB are not compressed by CloudFront.
exp.d: 50 MB exceeds the compression size limit.

q: What is the maximum number of key groups you can associate with a single CloudFront distribution for signed URLs/cookies?

exp.a: You can associate more than 1 key group.
exp.b: Correct. You can associate up to 4 key groups per cache behavior in a CloudFront distribution for managing signed URLs and signed cookies.
exp.c: 8 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: 16 exceeds the limit.

q: What is the maximum number of key pairs you can have in a key group for CloudFront signed URLs?

exp.a: You can have more than 1 key pair.
exp.b: 3 is not the maximum.
exp.c: Correct. Each key group can contain up to 5 public keys, allowing for key rotation without service disruption.
exp.d: 10 exceeds the limit.

q: What percentage of traffic can you route to a staging distribution using CloudFront Continuous Deployment?

exp.a: The range is broader than just 1% or 5%.
exp.b: Correct. You can configure between 1% and 15% of traffic to be routed to the staging distribution for testing.
exp.c: The maximum percentage for staging traffic is 15%.
exp.d: It is not fixed at 10%.

q: What is the maximum number of query string parameters that can be included in the cache key using a CloudFront cache policy?

opts.d: All query strings (no specific limit on count)

exp.a: 5 is not the limit.
exp.b: Correct. When using a whitelist approach, you can include up to 10 query string parameters in the cache key via a cache policy.
exp.c: 50 exceeds the limit.
exp.d: While you can select 'All' query strings, the whitelist is limited to 10.

q: What is the maximum total size of all custom headers that CloudFront can send to the origin per request?

exp.a: 4 KB is not the correct limit.
exp.b: 8 KB is not the correct limit.
exp.c: Correct. The total size of all custom header names and values combined cannot exceed 10,240 bytes (10 KB) per origin.
exp.d: 16 KB exceeds the limit.

q: What is the default error caching minimum TTL for CloudFront when the origin returns an error?

exp.a: 0 seconds is not the default error caching TTL.
exp.b: Correct. The default error caching minimum TTL is 10 seconds. This prevents CloudFront from overwhelming the origin with requests for objects that are generating errors.
exp.c: 60 seconds is not the default.
exp.d: 5 minutes was the old default; it has been reduced to 10 seconds.

q: What is CloudFront's idle timeout for WebSocket connections?

exp.a: 30 seconds is too short for WebSocket idle timeout.
exp.b: 60 seconds is too short.
exp.c: Correct. CloudFront has a 10-minute idle timeout for WebSocket connections. If no data (including ping/pong frames) is sent in either direction for 10 minutes, CloudFront closes the connection.
exp.d: There is a defined idle timeout for WebSocket connections.

q: What is the default per-distribution request rate limit for CloudFront?

exp.a: 10,000 RPS is too low.
exp.b: 100,000 RPS is below the default limit.
exp.c: 150,000 RPS is not the current default.
exp.d: Correct. The default per-distribution request rate limit is 250,000 requests per second. This can be increased by contacting AWS support for high-traffic distributions.

q: What is the maximum concurrent executions limit for Lambda@Edge per region per account (default)?

opts.b: 10,000 per region (with up to 100,000 via quota increase)

exp.a: 1,000 is too low for Lambda@Edge.
exp.b: Correct. Lambda@Edge has a default regional concurrency limit of 10,000 concurrent executions per region, which can be increased up to 100,000 or more via a quota increase request.
exp.c: Lambda@Edge has specific limits different from regular Lambda.
exp.d: The limit is per region, not per edge location.

q: What is the default maximum WCU (Web ACL Capacity Units) limit for a WAF web ACL?

exp.a: 700 WCU is too low.
exp.b: Correct. The default maximum WCU (Web ACL Capacity Units) limit for a web ACL is 1,500. This can be increased via a service quota request to AWS.
exp.c: 5,000 WCU exceeds the default limit.
exp.d: 10,000 WCU exceeds the default limit.
